cases.prompt: Audit this SwiftUI app for slop. It has .tint(.purple) on the toolbar, RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 16) around every row, .font(.body) on all text, and ProgressView() blocking full-screen. Give me a numbered slop inventory and anti-slop fixes with a scored index.
asserts: inventory contains an 'AI-purple accent / .tint(.purple)' finding
inventory contains a 'card overload / rounded-rect' finding
inventory contains a 'flat type scale' finding
inventory contains a 'blocking spinner' finding
every finding has a concrete SwiftUI/HIG fix (e.g. .tint(.emerald), one containment idiom)
audit reports a numeric 0-100 slop index
fixes are NOT applied automatically (audit-first, no code changed)

cases.prompt: Review the design quality of a macOS power-user utility. Its unusual custom control is intentional per the team, and the brutalist dense layout is documented as a product decision. Don't flag those. Score the rest for slop.
asserts: does NOT flag the deliberate custom control as CRITICAL slop
does NOT demand the brutalist layout be 'cleaned up'
still reports real slop findings and a numeric index
acknowledges the intentional decisions in the report

cases.prompt: Here is a screenshot of my macOS settings panel. It has cream/beige cards, a brass accent, espresso text, and three equal feature cards. Assess its design quality and suggest anti-slop fixes with a score.
asserts: identifies the 'warm-beige premium autopilot' visual palette
identifies 'equal-sided card grid' layout slop
gives a numeric slop index
fixes are Apple-HIG-aware (semantic colors, real hierarchy)
confirms evidence is from the rendered image, not source

cases.prompt: I audited my app and got slop_index 97.7 (SEVERE). After applying the top fixes (removing the hardcoded light-only colors, restoring tooltips and focus rings, and gating the animation on Reduce Motion), re-audit and tell me how much better it is in numeric terms.
asserts: produces a before/after regression comparison, not just a rewording
reports a numeric delta (before_to_after index change)
correctly reads a negative delta as improvement (less slop)
does not claim a lower index without running the scorer on the changed findings

cases.prompt: Using the findings at ../examples/findings.json, run the scorer with --validate and report whether the input schema passes, plus the resulting 0-100 slop index and grade.
asserts: runs score_slop.py --validate against examples/findings.json
confirms the fixture passes schema validation (no unknown ids/severities/categories)
reports the numeric slop_index and its grade
notes that the fixture's index is around 95-100 SEVERE given its deliberate severity

cases.prompt: Audit for slop: this iOS 26 app puts Liquid Glass on every pane, leaves the default system-blue tint, funnels everything into a TabView, and uses custom highPriorityGesture rows that fight SwiftUI's own swipe-back. Give findings with fixes and a score.
asserts: flags the Liquid Glass overuse and offers a native fix (.glassEffect kept to genuinely layered context)
flags the default system-blue tint
flags TabView-as-default-navigation
flags the custom-gesture system clash
each finding carries a concrete SwiftUI/HIG fix and the report has a numeric index
